summary: René Gothóni worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1970–1980) and held a post there from around 1975 to 2014, where he taught Ilkka Pyysiäinen.

René Grousset specialized in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology, having studied at the University of Montpellier. His posts included the Musée Guimet, École du Louvre, Musée Cernuschi as conservateur, and the Louvre Museum.

René Guénon was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He completed his education at Robert-Badinter School Complex (1902–1903), Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1904–1906), and the University of Paris (1914–1917).

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Berlin, SOAS, LSE, and Vienna under Koppers, Haekel, Bleichsteiner, Tucci, and Rock, earning his doctorate and habilitation, and served as wissenschaftlicher Beamter at Weltmuseum Wien (1958).
Reting Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied traditionally under Kalu Rinpoche and Chatral Sangye Dorje, and he taught Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama.
Rewa Prasad Dwivedi worked in Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, where he later served as Head of Sahityavidya from around 1977 to 1995.

Rewata Dhamma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, and earned a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

Richard A. Hutch worked in religious studies after studying at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).
Richard B. Martin worked in Indology and Tibetology. He held positions at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and as a South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at UC Berkeley, Harvard, and under Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center and served as its abbot from 1971 to 1984 before founding Dharma Sangha.
Richard Barron works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his traditional studies under Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bowring is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D at Cambridge. He held academic posts at Columbia, Princeton, and Cambridge, and served as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

Richard Carnac Temple, active in Indology and history, studied at Harrow and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited The Indian Antiquary, founded Panjab Notes and Queries, and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society.
Richard D. Mann works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2007).

Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at UCLA under mentor Robert Buswell and held posts at Dongguk University and Brigham Young University (attested 2019).

Richard Delbrueck was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Bonn (~1895–1899). He held professorships and academic posts at the University of Jena (~1911–1914), University of Giessen (~1922–1928), and University of Bonn (~1928–1940).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago in 2004 and served as an assistant professor at Indiana University (attested 2013).

Richard Fick was an Indologist who completed his promotion at Kiel University (1885–1888). He worked at the Kiel University Library, Prussian State Library, and directed Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932), serving also as honorary professor at Göttingen.

Richard Foltz is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, educated at the University of Utah and Harvard. He taught at Kuwait, Brown, Columbia, and Florida, and became Founding Director at Concordia University (~2006–2026).
Richard Fritzsche studied under Hermann Brockhaus from around 1873 to 1877. He served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.
